hints: Look closely at how options A and B list valves one by one, while C and D group them in pairs. Ask yourself, do the left and right sides of the heart work one after the other or at the same time?

Remember what drives a valve to open: pressure on one side becomes higher than on the other. Think about when atria contract together and when ventricles contract together, and which pair of valves each contraction opens.
walkthrough:
**Recall what makes any heart valve open**

Valves are passive flaps. They open when pressure behind them is higher than pressure in front of them.

So we just need to ask, when is atrial pressure high, and when is ventricular pressure high?

**Link valve opening to the two main contractions**

First, the two atria contract together in atrial systole. This raises atrial pressure above ventricular pressure, so both atrioventricular valves open together.

Next, the two ventricles contract together in ventricular systole. This raises ventricular pressure above artery pressure, so both semilunar valves open together.

**Pick the sequence that matches**

That gives a simple two-stage sequence: both AV valves open first to fill the ventricles, then both semilunar valves open to eject blood.

Only option D shows left and right AV valves together, followed by aortic and pulmonary semilunar valves together.

options.A: Incorrect because it separates right and left sides in time. The two sides of the heart contract in synchrony, so valves do not open right side then left side.
options.B: Incorrect because it also lists all four valves opening one after another. Atrial systole and ventricular systole happen on both sides at once, not left then right.
options.C: Incorrect because it pairs an AV valve with a semilunar valve on the same side. An AV valve and a semilunar valve on the same side are never open together, as that would let blood flow straight back through the ventricle.
options.D: Correct because both AV valves open together during atrial systole to fill ventricles, then both semilunar valves open together during ventricular systole to pump blood to lungs and body.
